chunks: Ahmad ibn Mihran, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, who said:

The people in Mecca were struck by many lightning bolts during one of the years, and a great number of people died from that. So I entered upon Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him), and he began speaking without me asking him: 'It is befitting for the drowned one and the one struck by lightning that they be awaited for three days; they are not buried unless a breeze comes from him indicating his death.' I said, 'May I be your ransom, it seems as if you are informing me that many people have been buried alive.' He said, 'Yes, O Ali! Many people have been buried alive; they did not die except inside their graves.'
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling for burying those killed by lightning or drowning?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the fiqh of *istishab* (presumption of continuity) for those killed by natural disasters like lightning or drowning, prescribing a three-day waiting period to ensure death has occurred before burial. This ruling highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on distinguishing between the moment of physical cessation and the actual state of death, noting that many victims succumbed only after being interred, thus underscoring the importance of careful observation in ritual practices.

en.hubeali: Ahmad Bin Mihran, from Muhammad Bin Ali, from Ali Bin Abu Hamza who said,

‘The people at Makkah were hit by a lot of lightning during a year from the year. A lot of people died from that. So I went over to Abu Ibrahim<sup>asws</sup> (7<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>), and he<sup>asws</sup> said initiating from without me asking him<sup>asws</sup>: ‘It is befitting for the drowned one and the one struck by lightning that they should be awaited with for three (days) not being buried exept if a smell comes out from him evidencing upon his death’. I said, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! It is as if you<sup>asws</sup> are informing me that a lot of the people have been buried alive!’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes, O Ali! A lot of people have been buried alive. They did not died except inside their graves’.
en.sarwar: 6. Ahmad ibn Mehran has narrated from Muhammad ibn Ali from Ali ibn abu Hamzah who has said the following:

“In one of the years many people in Makkah died because of a great deal of lightning and thunder. I visited abu Ibrahim, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, and he, without asking, initiated stating, ‘It is proper to delay for three days the burial of one who has died because of drowning and sudden shock unless the spread of smell proves his death.’ I then said, ‘I pray to Allah to keep my soul in service for your cause, are you telling me that many people are buried alive? He (the Imam) said, ‘Yes, O Ali, many people were buried alive and they did not die but in their graves.’”
